heading: Representation of United States under Convention

children.heading: Appointments, generally
children.text: The Secretary shall appoint not more than 3 individuals to serve as the representatives of the United States on the Commission, who shall each—
be known as a “United States Commissioner to the Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Organization”; and
serve at the pleasure of the Secretary.
The Secretary shall ensure that of the individuals serving as Commissioners—
at least 1 is appointed from among representatives of the commercial fishing industry;
1 (but no more than 1) is an official of the Government; and
1, other than the individual appointed under clause (ii), is a voting member of the New England Fishery Management Council.
The Secretary may not appoint as a Commissioner an individual unless the individual is knowledgeable and experienced concerning the fishery resources to which the Convention applies.
The term of an individual appointed as a Commissioner—
shall be specified by the Secretary at the time of appointment; and
may not exceed 4 years.
An individual who is not a Government official may not serve more than 2 consecutive terms as a Commissioner.

children.heading: Appointment
children.text: The Secretary may, for any anticipated absence of a duly appointed Commissioner, designate an individual to serve as an Alternate Commissioner.

children.heading: Functions
children.text: An Alternate Commissioner may exercise all powers and perform all duties of the Commissioner for whom the Alternate Commissioner is designated.

children.heading: Appointment
children.text: The Secretary shall appoint not more than 3 individuals to serve as the representatives of the United States on the Scientific Council, who shall each be known as a “United States Representative to the Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Organization Scientific Council”.
The Secretary may not appoint an individual as a Representative unless the individual is knowledgeable and experienced concerning the scientific issues dealt with by the Scientific Council.
The Secretary shall appoint as a Representative at least 1 individual who is an official of the Government.

children.heading: Term
children.text: An individual appointed as a Representative—
shall serve for a term of not to exceed 4 years, as specified by the Secretary at the time of appointment;
may be reappointed; and
shall serve at the pleasure of the Secretary.

children.heading: Appointment
children.text: The Secretary may, for any anticipated absence of a duly appointed Representative, designate an individual to serve as an Alternate Representative.

children.heading: Functions
children.text: An Alternate Representative may exercise all powers and perform all duties of the Representative for whom the Alternate Representative is designated.

tree.heading: Experts and advisers
tree.text: The Commissioners, Alternate Commissioners, Representatives, and Alternate Representatives may be accompanied at meetings of the Organization by experts and advisers.

children.heading: In general
children.text: In carrying out their functions under the Convention, Commissioners, Alternate Commissioners, Representatives, and Alternate Representatives shall—
coordinate with the appropriate Regional Fishery Management Councils established by section 1852 of this title; and
consult with the committee established under section 5607 of this title.

children.heading: Relationship to other law
children.text: Chapter 10 of title 5 shall not apply to coordination and consultations under this subsection.

notes.heading: Short Title of 2016 Amendment
notes.text: Pub. L. 114–327, title V, § 501(a), Dec. 16, 2016, 130 Stat. 1995, provided that: “This title [amending this section and sections 5602 to 5604, 5606, 5607, 5609, and 5610 of this title and repealing section 5612 of this title] may be cited as the ‘Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Convention Amendments Act’.”

notes.heading: Short Title
notes.text: Pub. L. 104–43, title II, § 201, Nov. 3, 1995, 109 Stat. 377, provided that: “This title [enacting this chapter] may be cited as the ‘Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Convention Act of 1995’.”
